description: Mask filtering using a real per-pixel depth test (not a stored/dataset depth channel -- ShapeR's pkl schema has none; depth here is rendered on the fly from the ground-truth and distractor meshes through the same cameras).

filtering_procedure.method: Render the GT target mesh's depth AND the distractor mesh's depth through the same batch cameras (augment.render_through_views). Remove mask pixels wherever the distractor is nearer the camera than the target: hit_o & (depth_o > 0) & (depth_t<=0 | depth_o<depth_t).
filtering_procedure.bug_caught_before_use: The undefended version (target silhouette only, no depth test) covered 76-100% of the distractor's pixels, because the distractor stands in front of the target -- the 'oracle' mask would have told the model exactly where the distractor was, the opposite of its purpose.
filtering_procedure.verification: updated_2/mask_vs_leak/verify_masks.py scores both the SAM2 mask and the depth-verified oracle mask against rendered GT silhouettes (target_hit / pot_hit / pot_share) before any downstream number is trusted.

target_retention_and_distractor_removal_.method: Non-depth alternative for comparison: split the point cloud with segment_by_support_v2, then prompt SAM2 with target points as POSITIVE clicks and intruder points as NEGATIVE clicks.
target_retention_and_distractor_removal_.note: This is the 'fixed' arm in the three_arms.py comparison below; distinct from the depth-verified 'oracle' arm.

measured_result_depth_verified_oracle_vs.condition: image-mode clutter (distractor in photos only, absent from the point cloud) -- the one condition where the mask channel could possibly matter
measured_result_depth_verified_oracle_vs.source: updated_2/mask_vs_leak/outputs/clean_test/scores.json, aggregated (see docs/provenance.md for the aggregation command)

oracle.desc: depth-verified mask, distractor excluded by a real depth test

measured_result_support_segmenter_fix_vs.condition: mixed object set, three_arms.py (control=guidance off / stock=today's mask / fixed=support-segmenter + SAM2 negative clicks)

conclusion_and_limitation: Even a PERFECT, ground-truth depth-verified mask only beats SAM2's own guess by ~0.11 points of Leak% (1.913 vs 2.023), far short of removing the leakage (off: 2.345). The support-segmenter fix shows the same small-and-inconclusive pattern (8.305 -> 8.292 -> 8.146). Mask ACCURACY is therefore not the bottleneck: the model's mask-conditioning channel is too weak to act decisively on an accurate mask, consistent with B's null multi-seed verdict on mask guidance in general.
